newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian union calls for Colston police probe.
newsitem.headline: Australian union calls for Colston police probe.

text.p: Australia's national police union said on Tuesday police should investigate key independent Senator Mal Colston over allegations he had abused allowances.
Australian Federal Police Association secretary Chris Eaton said the row had become politicised and only an independent police probe could clear the air.
"Nobody knows who to believe as a result of this contrived environment of media frenzy and political point-scoring," Eaton said in a statement.
"The only way that we can know the facts is for federal agents to ask questions of those concerned, and to make a detailed analysis of the circumstances and documents," Eaton said.

Colston, who defected from the Labor Party last year to sit as an independent, is one of two independent senators the government has relied on to pass controversial legislation through the upper house Senate, where the government is in a minority.
Last month, he repaid A$6,880 after a Senate inquiry found he had claimed travelling allowance for travel he had not undertaken.
Colston denies all allegations of abuse and said the discrepancy resulted from a book-keeping mistake by a staffer.
A departmental investigation into allegations against Colston is continuing.
Eaton urged Prime Minister John Howard to refer the allegations against Colston to the Australian Federal Police, the national police force.
Howard has said he would insist on a police investigation if he received advice Colston had broken the law.
Democrat leader Cheryl Kernot has said her party could move a no-confidence motion against Colston when the Senate resumes in May 6.
If found guilty of fraud Colston would be forced out of the Senate and replaced by a Labor candidate.
This could cast doubt over government legislation, including its budget for financial 1997/98, due to be announced on May 13.
